extra.message: User-controlled query parameter 'region' is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string passed to AppDataSource.query(). The ILIKE clauses interpolate ${region} without parameterization, allowing SQL injection by authenticated staff.

profile.letterheadFilename (settable by the borrower via PUT /api/borrowers/my, allowedFields includes 'letterheadFilename') is joined into path.join(LETTERHEAD_DIR, filename) and read with fs.readFileSync without any path confinement. A value like '../../etc/passwd' reads arbitrary files off disk.

noteFileName from the request body is joined directly into path.join(COMPLIANCE_STAGING_DIR, noteFileName) and written with fs.writeFileSync without path.basename or confinement. Allows writing arbitrary files outside the staging directory (path traversal write).

fileName from the request body is joined directly into path.join(PRODUCT_ASSETS_DIR, fileName) and written with fs.writeFileSync without path.basename or confinement. A traversal filename can write arbitrary files on the server.

The 'format' query parameter (outputFormat) is interpolated into a shell command executed via execSync() without validation or allowlisting. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary OS commands. Contrast with renderPortfolioSummary which uses execFileSync with shell:false and an allowlist.
The 'x-redirect-url' header (or the Referer header) is used verbatim in res.redirect(nextUrl) with no validation against a safe allowlist. This allows an open redirect to arbitrary external sites.

The 'x-template-source-url' header is fetched directly without any hostname allowlisting. An admin-level caller can use the server to make requests to internal services (SSRF). Contrast with previewExternalTemplateSource which validates against ALLOWED_TEMPLATE_HOSTS.

The 'badge_id' query parameter is concatenated into an LDAP filter string `(uid=${badgeId})` without RFC 4515 escaping. LDAP injection can alter the filter semantics. Contrast with verifyComplianceGroupMembership which applies ldapEscape() to user input.

JWT_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded value 'loan-origination-jwt-secret-dev-only'. If JWT_SECRET is not set in the environment, any attacker who knows this constant can forge valid tokens (including admin tokens), bypassing authentication and authorization.

COUNTEROFFER_TOKEN_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded value 'counteroffer-token-secret-dev-only'. The encryption key used for counteroffer resume tokens is predictable, allowing forgery of counteroffer tokens.

LEDGER_SYNC_SECRET and PAYOUT_DRAFT_SECRET fall back to hardcoded dev-only values ('ledger-sync-partner-secret-dev-only', 'payout-draft-secret-dev-only'). These keys sign ledger/disbursement session tokens and encrypt payout drafts; with the defaults known, tokens can be forged.

POST /api/payment-accounts/ledger-sync/start has no authentication middleware yet issues a valid signed sessionToken for any supplied accountId. Combined with the hardcoded secret, this lets an unauthenticated caller mint ledger/disbursement sync session tokens.

POST /api/payment-accounts/ledger-sync has no authentication middleware and verifies the session token with jwt.verify(..., { ignoreExpiration: true }), disabling token expiry checks. Tokens are also verifiable with the hardcoded fallback secret.

POST /api/payment-accounts/disbursement-sync (funds-movement reconciliation) has no authentication middleware. Any caller can resume a disbursement sync session if they can produce a token signed with the (hardcoded) LEDGER_SYNC_SECRET.

GET /api/payment-accounts/partner-status has no authentication and grants access based solely on the client-supplied 'x-partner-role' header equalling 'ledger-service'. An attacker can set this header to be treated as an authorized ledger partner (CWE-862/287).

When the caller sends header 'x-branch-context: expanded', the error handler returns error.message, error.stack, and request params in the response body, leaking internal implementation details and stack traces to a client-controlled condition.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: markDeviceTrusted sets the 'sessionId' cookie via res.cookie without httpOnly, secure, or sameSite attributes, leaving the session token exposed to JavaScript/XSS and transmitted over insecure channels. Contrast with startSupportSession which sets httpOnly/secure/sameSite.
